decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through contacts extend the firm's core competence and cost little to keep alongside existing production, while demand for advanced packaging keeps their upside open.
Carrier wafers are a low-cost extension of the established offer that fits the stated strategic direction toward reusable carriers and thin-wafer handling, so keeping the option open is cheap.
The Cu-interposer is a flagship aligned with growing wafer-level packaging demand, and its value is still uncertain but potentially large, which justifies keeping the option alive.
The off-the-shelf brand sits close to the core business and uses existing inventory and processes, so keeping it costs little and it serves as a sales channel.

Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the core and more costly to pursue, but uncertainty is still unresolved and there is no clear negative signal, so the option is held for now under close scrutiny.
